text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) leader Mesut Yilmaz attacked in Budapest hotel lobby.
- Pope's would-be killer Mehmet Ali Agca says late gangster at centre of scandal in Turkey helped him flee the country on the way to Italy for assassination bid.
- Left-wing party protests at the government's plans to restrict the media.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says security scandal will not be covered up.
- Erbakan's Welfare Party plans to ban one of two national lotteries.
- Erbakan to reveal new package of economic measures today.
- Professor says organised crime syndicates control sector of the economy worth 345 trillion lira.
- Two sons of late president Turgut Ozal regain control of Kanal 6 television channel in lightning raid on channel's headquarters.
